requirements.title: Type parameter inquiries interrogate data-object type parameters for intrinsic and derived types
requirements.definition: A type parameter inquiry is used to inquire about a type parameter of a data object. It applies to both intrinsic and derived types. The inquired entity is a type parameter: intrinsic type parameters are defined by the intrinsic type clauses, and derived type parameters are integer kind or length parameters from 7.5.3.1; this subclause does not create a non-integer data component or a structure component.

pending.data-object-parameter-inquiry: PENDING positive-control source: declare a data object and use a type parameter inquiry in an expression primary context, comparing the result with an independent integer literal. The object is otherwise used normally so the inquiry is not confused with a component value.
pending.intrinsic-kind-parameter: PENDING positive-control source: inquire a%kind for an intrinsic REAL or COMPLEX object with a known selected kind, comparing to KIND(a) or a separately declared kind literal where support is established. KIND intrinsic ownership remains 16.9.118.
pending.intrinsic-length-parameter: PENDING positive-control source: CHARACTER(5) :: s; compare s%len with integer literal 5 and LEN(s) as a cross-check, while treating LEN intrinsic semantics as a dependency rather than the primary oracle.
pending.derived-kind-parameter: PENDING positive-control source: define a parameterized derived type with INTEGER,KIND :: k and object TYPE(t(k=kind_literal)) :: x; compare x%k with the declared integer literal. Component definitions and parameterized type syntax remain 7.5-owned.
pending.derived-length-parameter: PENDING positive-control source: define a derived type with INTEGER,LEN :: n and object with explicit n value; compare x%n with the integer literal and use a component whose bounds depend on n only as a non-vacuous control. Allocation or defaulting details remain 7.5/9.7 dependencies.
pending.integer-parameter-result-boundary: PENDING source plan: place intrinsic and derived parameter inquiries in integer expression contexts such as array bounds or integer comparisons with literal oracles. Do not infer a separate result-kind rule beyond the kind of the type parameter as defined by 7.4.1 and 7.5.3.1 until independently reviewed.

requirements.title: A type parameter inquiry is a designator followed by percent and a type parameter name
requirements.definition: The syntactic form type-param-inquiry is designator followed by percent and a type-param-name. The left operand is an existing designator, not an arbitrary expression, and the right token is a type parameter name whose validity is constrained by C923.

pending.designator-percent-name-form: PENDING positive-control source: use object%kind or object%len with a declared object and compare the inquiry value to an independent integer literal. The percent-name spelling is the only type-param-inquiry form credited.
pending.simple-object-designator: PENDING positive-control source: simple intrinsic or derived object name on the left of %kind/%len/%parameter, with an integer literal oracle. The object is declared before the inquiry.
pending.array-element-designator: PENDING positive-control source: use a(2)%kind or b(10)%kind where a/b is an array of objects with a known type parameter; compare with the expected integer literal. Array-element validity remains 9.5-owned.
pending.expression-left-operand-rejected: PENDING diagnostic/control source: attempt (a)%kind or (a+b)%kind where no R901 designator alternative applies; repair to a declared designator a%kind and compare the repaired value to a literal. If parentheses are accepted as a designator by another owner, reassign the facet during review.
pending.missing-percent-rejected: PENDING diagnostic/control source: spell a kind or a.kind in an otherwise eligible inquiry context; repair only to a%kind and compare the integer result to a literal. The type-param-name is valid so the failure is form, not C923 name lookup.

requirements.title: The queried name is a type parameter of the declared type of the designated object
requirements.definition: For an R916 type-param-inquiry, type-param-name shall be the name of a type parameter of the declared type of the object designated by the designator. The test is against the object's declared type, not an unrelated component name and not a parameter introduced only by a possible dynamic type extension.

pending.intrinsic-kind-name: PENDING positive-control source: use x%kind for an intrinsic numeric or logical object with known kind and compare to an integer literal or KIND(x) dependency. The plan records that KIND is a type parameter name, not a component.
pending.character-len-name: PENDING positive-control source: CHARACTER(7) :: s; use s%len and compare to integer literal 7. The character object's length parameter is known independently from its declaration.
pending.derived-type-parameter-name: PENDING positive-control source: parameterized derived type t(k,n) with INTEGER,KIND :: k and INTEGER,LEN :: n; use obj%k and obj%n with integer literal oracles. The component list uses different names to prevent accidental component lookup.
pending.ordinary-component-name-rejected: PENDING diagnostic/control source: derived type has ordinary component value but no type parameter named value; attempt obj%value as a type-param-inquiry in a context where structure-component semantics would not be selected, then repair to obj%k. The valid control observes the integer type parameter literal.
pending.undeclared-parameter-name-rejected: PENDING diagnostic/control source: attempt obj%missing for a type with known parameters k and n; repair to obj%k or obj%n and compare to the declared literal. The name missing is not an ordinary component either, isolating the C923 lookup predicate.
pending.declared-type-not-dynamic-extension: PENDING diagnostic/control source: CLASS(parent) designator whose dynamic allocation may be child with an extra type parameter, attempt inquiry of the child-only parameter without SELECT TYPE; repair by querying a parent-declared parameter or by using a SELECT TYPE owner. Literal parameter values distinguish declared-type lookup from dynamic-type execution.

requirements.title: Deferred type parameters of unassociated pointers or unallocated allocatables are not inquired about
requirements.definition: A deferred type parameter of a pointer that is not associated, or of an allocatable variable that is unallocated, shall not be inquired about. The restriction is about deferred type parameters and the pointer association or allocatable allocation status at the inquiry; it does not prohibit inquiries of nondeferred parameters merely because the object is a pointer or allocatable.

pending.associated-pointer-deferred-parameter: PENDING positive-control source: associate a pointer with a target whose deferred LEN parameter has a known value, then inquire p%len and compare with an integer literal after proving association on the executed path. No unassociated pointer branch is executed.
pending.unassociated-pointer-deferred-parameter: PENDING diagnostic-policy/source plan: construct a pointer with deferred type parameter that is statically or deliberately unassociated, and attempt the inquiry only in a non-executed or diagnostic harness; repair by associating it with a target of known parameter value. Because association status can be runtime-valued, no unconditional static diagnostic duty is claimed.
pending.allocated-allocatable-deferred-parameter: PENDING positive-control source: allocate an allocatable character or parameterized derived object with explicit deferred parameter value, then inquire it and compare with an integer literal. Reached execution confirms the allocation before inquiry.
pending.unallocated-allocatable-deferred-paramet: PENDING diagnostic-policy/source plan: attempt to inquire a deferred parameter of an unallocated allocatable only under a harness that treats the source as nonconforming without reading a result; repair by allocating with a known parameter and compare the repaired inquiry to a literal. Static rejection is not required unless another numbered owner applies.
pending.nondeferred-parameter-control: PENDING positive-control source: pointer or allocatable object with nondeferred type parameter or established allocation/association is queried with an integer literal oracle. This isolates that p2 is triggered by deferred-parameter status combined with unassociated or unallocated state.

review_rationale: Independent source review in doc/source_audits/batch_089.json reads all six original 9.4.5 units and their23 fine units, including note2 on the following physical page, and confirms that R916 supplies the designator%type-param-name form and that C923 requires the type-param-name to be a parameter of the declared type of the designated object rather than its dynamic type. Paragraph p2 prohibits inquiring about a deferred type parameter of an unassociated pointer or an unallocated allocatable; that condition depends on runtime status, so it keeps a non-required diagnostic obligation and no plan executes such an inquiry. NOTE 1 stays informative here: the non-variable, primary-only and scalar-result statements are recorded without being promoted to locally owned requirements or silently dropped. All22 facets remain pending source plans; no case, execution, oracle or fixture approval is created.
